standard_title: Safety of Toys - Part 1: Safety Aspects Related to Mechanical and Physical Properties
clause_title: Scope and Toys Quality Control Order
text: Applies to all toys intended for use by children under 14 years of age. Under the Toys (Quality Control) Order issued by DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce & Industry, all toys manufactured, imported, or distributed in India must compulsorily conform to IS 9873 and IS 15644 and carry the ISI Mark under Scheme-I certification. Foreign and domestic toy manufacturers must obtain a BIS licence before market release.

standard_title: Safety of Toys - Part 1: Safety Aspects Related to Mechanical and Physical Properties
clause_title: Small Parts and Choking Hazards (<36 months)
text: Toys intended for children under 36 months of age, and their detachable components, shall not fit entirely within the small parts test cylinder (diameter 31.7 mm, truncated cylinder angle 45°, depth 57.1 mm) under zero or specified force. Any small part that fits inside poses a fatal choking risk and constitutes immediate non-conformance.

standard_title: Safety of Toys - Part 1: Safety Aspects Related to Mechanical and Physical Properties
clause_title: Accessible Sharp Edges and Sharp Points
text: Accessible edges shall not present an unreasonable risk of injury. Sharp edges are verified using a rotating mandrel covered with PTFE adhesive tape under 6 N force. Sharp points are evaluated using a sharp point tester with an indicator light triggering when the point penetrates deeper than 0.5 mm into a 1.0 mm x 1.15 mm rectangular orifice under 4.5 N spring pressure.

standard_title: Safety of Toys - Part 2: Flammability Requirements
clause_title: Flammability of Soft Toys, Costumes and Wigs
text: Stuffed soft toys, disguise costumes, and play tents shall not produce flash fire upon contact with a small test flame. The rate of flame spread across plush fabrics or simulated hair shall not exceed 30 mm/s when ignited for 3 seconds with a standardized gas micro-burner.

standard_title: Safety of Toys - Part 3: Migration of Certain Elements (Chemical Toxicology)
text: The maximum acceptable levels of elemental migration from toy materials (paints, plastics, coatings, modelling clay) into 0.07 mol/L hydrochloric acid simulant shall not exceed: Lead (Pb): 90 mg/kg; Cadmium (Cd): 75 mg/kg; Mercury (Hg): 60 mg/kg; Arsenic (As): 25 mg/kg; Barium (Ba): 1000 mg/kg; Chromium (Cr): 60 mg/kg; Antimony (Sb): 60 mg/kg; Selenium (Se): 500 mg/kg. Tested via Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS).

standard_title: Safety of Electric Toys - Electrical Safety Requirements
text: Electric toys shall not be powered by a supply voltage exceeding 24 V DC or AC equivalent (Safety Extra Low Voltage - SELV). Battery compartments must prevent children from easily extracting button cells without a screwdriver/coin-operated dual locking mechanism, and must withstand drop testing without battery expulsion.
mandatory_status: Electrical Safety Test for Battery/Powered Toys
